11 * 15 * 78 * 6 * 18 * 160

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number.

8 : 81 : : 12 ? : : 11 : 144
questions.solution:
The logic is:

8 : 81 → 8 : (8 + 1)²

11 : 144 → 11 : (11 + 1)²

Similarly,

12 : ? → 12 : (12 + 1)²

⇒ ? = 169

Hence, ‘169’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1. All boys are robots.

2. All girls are robots.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some robots are boys.

II. No robot is a girl.

III. Some robots are girls.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
All conclusions I, II and III follow.
Only conclusion I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3db8bfcc4d2b78fb4974a2d5d6c53ed091fa31133fd205cfa6b838d3038c5c8.png] 

I. Some robots are boys. → True (As all boys are robots so some robots will be definitely boys)

II. No robot is a girl. → False (As all girls are robots so some robots are girls, hence false)

III. Some robots are girls → True (As all girls are robots so some robots will be definitely girls)

Hence, only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.question: Four number-pairs have been given. Out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different from the rest.
questions.solution:
The logic is:

The logic followed here is:

First number × ( First number+ 1) = second number

1) 11 : 142 → 11 × (11 + 1) = 132 ≠ 142

2) 22 : 506 → 22 × (22 + 1) = 506

3) 17 : 306 → 17 × (17 + 1) = 306

4) 14 : 210 → 14 × (14 + 1) = 210

Hence, ‘11 : 142’ is the odd one out.

questions.question:
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary?

1. Dovetail

2. Domestic

3. Dominate

4. Donate

5. Dorsal
questions.solution:
The correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary is:

2. Dom**__e__**stic

3. Dom**__i__**nate

4. Do**__n__**ate

5. Do**__r__**sal

1. Do**__v__**etail

Hence, ‘2, 3, 4, 5,1 ’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 29 January 2003 is a Wednesday, then what day of the week will be 26 February 2005?
questions.solution:
29 January 2003 is a Wednesday

Number of odd days between 29th January 2003 to 26th February 2005 = (2 + 0 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3) + 2 + (3 + 26) = 59

59 ÷ 7, we get 3 as remainder.

3 days after Wednesday is Saturday.

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/LtGj6bPC3MU4pCFyLnXBpJVwZXVDMBz5wS3reWirRd7PjjRdlDLz-8Jk5zgwQryUyr9ar6_fLYm3XChgSRobFdSvoPg--RujRdwN-RyMXKU0RmHwghjTePQ0wqYiRe6hUJA_i3Ry] 

**29 January 2003 ⇒ Wednesday.**

(Number of odd days from 29 January 2003 to 29 January 2004 is 1)

**29 January 2004 ⇒ Thursday**

(Since February 2004 have 29 days, Number of odd days from 29 January 2004 to 29 January 2005 is 2)

**29 January 2005 ⇒ Saturday **

Number of odd days from 29 January 2005 to 26 February 2005 is 28. i.e. 0 odd days.

**26 February 2005 **⇒ Saturday

Hence, **‘Saturday**’ is the correct answer.
